Reference Petition Under Section 30/31 Of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 J U D
G M E N T / Awa

R D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

The present reference under Section 30-31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 along with memorandum of interested persons and compensation amount of Rs. 25,09,675 was received from the office of Land Acquisition Collector pertaining to Award No. 16/2005-06 of Mubarakpur Dabas in respect of acquisition of land, vide preliminary notification under Section 4 of the Act dated 21.03.2003.
The reference was forwarded for ascertaining the compensation amongst the interested person, in respect of Khasra Nos 15/1 min (4-16) village Mubarakpur LAC 3/2016 UOI.
Vs. Gram Sabha Mubarakpur Dabas & Ors Page no. 2 of 9 VIKRAM Date:

Dabas as the awarded compensation was assessed in favour of Gram Sabha Mubarakpur Dabas (Respondent/IP No.1) being the recorded owner of the land at item no. 467 of the Naksha Muntjamin of the award, but not released for objection of IP No.
2 to 5.
The reference was received in the Court on 11.11.2011.
2. Notices of the reference were issued to all the concerned parties.

On service of summons,
Interested Persons put in their appearance on 04.01.2012.
3. Claim Petitions by interested parties were filed on 03.05.2012.
In its claim petition IP no. 1 claimed that IP no. 1 is the recorded owner of the land and was in possession of the land till it was acquired under the award.
Therefore, only IP no.1 is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text:
Per contra, IP no. 2 to 5, in their claim petition, stated that the land was jointly owned by IP no. 2,
3 and Ram Kanwar, all sons of Sh. Surat Singh and after the death of Sh. Ram Kanwar his share was inherited by IP No. 4 and 5.
It is stated that the land is ancestral land of IP no. 2 to 5 and they have been in possession and cultivation of the land.
However, in some ex-parte proceedings conducted u/S 81 DLR Act the Land was vested with the Gram Sabha.
It is stated that IP no. 2 to 5 have challenged the the vesting of land with Gram Sabha and same was pending till the land was acquire.
However, till the date of acquisition of land the same was in continuous undisturbed possession of IP no.2 to 5.
Therefore, IP no. 2 to 5 are entitled for compensation and not IP no.1.
LAC 3/2016 UOI. Vs. Gram Sabha Mubarakpur Dabas & Ors Page no. 3 of 9

VIKRAM Date:
5.

On the basis of rival claims made in the respective petitions, on 03.05.2012, following issues were framed:
1. Which of the IP is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent?
2. Relief.
6.
In Evidence IP no.1 produced 4 witnesses.
7. IP1W1 Sh. Sant Kumar from BDO Office Kanjhawala produced the Karwahi Register and LR Form 37 and deposed that there is no allotment on behalf of IP no.1 to IP no. 2 to 5.
However, said report or form was not exhibited and in cross examination IP1W1 stated that he is not aware if the original Gram Sabha Land is recorded in LR Form 37 or not.
He had no knowledge if there was any proceeding under section 81 and the land in the name of Gram Sabha in LR From 37 was recorded pursuant to proceeding u/S 81 DLR Act.
8. IP1W2 Sh. Karan Singh from DC Office Kanjhawala produced the Khasra Gbirdawari Ex.IP1W2/A for the year 2001 and 2002 as per which Gram Sabha is shown as the Bhumidar of Khasra No. 15/1.
9. IP1W3 Sh. Jai Bhagwan from the office of LAC proved the possession proceedings Ex.IP1W3/1.
In cross examination he deposed that LAC had not taken possession from BDO.

10.

IP1W4 Sh. Karan Singh from DC Office Kanjhawala proved the Khasra Girdawaris of Khasra No.
15/1, for the year 2002 to 2005 as Ex.IP1W4/1 to IP1W4/3 which is in the name of IP1.
In cross examination he admitted that there is no entry of any structure built on the land nor is there any crop shown.
11. On behalf of IP no. 2 to 5 only two witnesses were examined.

12. IP2-5W1 Ramesh Kumar Verma Naib Tehsildar SDM Office Rohini Division proved the record of case no. 1234/RA/SV/99 as Ex.IP2-5W1/1.
13.
IP No. 2-5 had also summoned the record of case no. 204/RA/94 on which SH. Narender Kumar, Record Keeper Revenue Dept., Tis Hazari appeared and stated that said file is not consigned to record room.

14. Therefore IP no.2 examined himself as IP2-5W3 and filed his affidavit Ex.IP2-5W3/A,
reiterating the claim of IP no. 2 to 5 and placed reliance on Khasra Girdawris for the year 1992-1993 and 1993-94 and proved them as Ex.IP2-5W3/1 and Ex.IP2- 5W3/2.

He also deposed in affidavit that the khasra girdawaris reproduced by him shows that the IP no. 2 -5 were the Bhumidar of the land till 1994 and they were cultivating the crop as such there was no violation committed by IP no.
2 to 5 to initiate proceedings u/S 81 DLR Act and vest the land with IP no.1.

He also deposed that vesting of land with IP no.1 was done on the basis of false report of Halka Patwari and they had already filed LAC 3/2016 UOI. Vs. Gram Sabha Mubarakpur Dabas & Ors Page no. 5 of 9 VIKRAM Date:
application under Appendix 6 Rule 14 of DLR Act to restore the land in their name but the same could not be done as the land was acquired before disposal of their application.

sentences.text: In cross examination this witnesses admitted that /land was vested with Gram Sabha vide order dated 17.01.1995 in case no. 204/RA/94

however, he denied that when possession was taken by LAC the land was lying vacant and in possession of IP no.1.
15.
I have heard the arguments and perused the record carefully.
16. Ex.IP2-5W3/1 and Ex.IP2-5W3/2 show that the IP no. 2 to 5 were bhumidar of the land and in cultivation.
Admittedly, the RA appears to have vested the land with IP no. 1 vide order dated 17.01.1995 in case no. 204/RO/94.

It has been claimed and deposed on behalf of IP no. 2 to 5 that the proceedings u/s 81 DLR Act were illegal and done on the basis of false report of halka Patwari and also because IP no. 2-5 were not given hearing before the order dated 17.01.1995.
Surprisingly IP no. 1 has not controverted this statement and deposition, in cross examination of IP2-5W3.

The IP no. 2-5 would refer to Khasra Girdawaris proved by them as well as by IP no.1 and also the Uoi (Mubarakpur Dabas) vs G.S.Mubarakpur Dabas Ors(1605-06) on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127928355/
4 possession proceedings to show that there was no such activity conducted on the land by erecting any structure or any other activity showing change in usage of land to justify the proceedings u/S 81 DLR Act.

sentences.text: The onus was, therefore, on the IP no. 1 to show any justifiable ground for proceeding u/S 81 DLR Act.
However, the IP no.1 did not even try to bring such justification on record.
The IP no.2-5 even tried to summon the record of that proceedings LAC 3/2016 UOI. Vs. Gram Sabha Mubarakpur Dabas & Ors Page no. 6 of 9 VIKRAM Date:

entities.text: LAC 3/2016 UOI. Vs. Gram Sabha Mubarakpur Dabas & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: but it was found not consigned to record room.
Even at the stage of arguments when this court called for record of that file same was not produced by SDM concerned.

17. Ld. Counsel for IP no.2-5 would, however, place reliance on Hardwari Lal Vs Rai Singh 2009 (107) DRJ 39(DB) and Ahad Brothers Vs State Of MP AIR 2005 SC 355 and submit that even if it is assumed that the proceedings u/S 81 were correct mere assertion of the Gram Sabha that it is Bhumidar would not entitle it for compensation and had the Gram Sabha was actually the owner of the land the state had no reason to acquire its own land.
18.

entities.text: Hardwari Lal Vs Rai Singh 2009 (107) DRJ 39(DB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ahad Brothers Vs State Of MP AIR 2005 SC 355
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The documents proved on record shows that the land was vacant at the time of its taking possession by LAC and IPW3 have categorically admitted that the LAC had not taken the possession of land from BDO.
It is the BDO who is custodian of the land.
If the land was possessed by Gram Sabha LAC would have taken possession of the land from BDO.
Possession proceedings dated 04.04.2006 records that when the possession of land was taken there was no one present from the side of villagers or from the side of Gram Sabha.
It would either mean that no villager was present at the time of taking possession or their presence was not marked.
IP1W3 has not deposed that all the land possessed vide proceedings dated 04.04.2006 were Gram Sabha Land, therefore, if there was any piece of land possessed by Gram Sabha BDO must have been present.
LAC 3/2016 UOI. Vs. Gram Sabha Mubarakpur Dabas & Ors Page no. 7 of 9 VIKRAM Date:

sentences.text: 19 . On the other hand proceedings under section 81 DLR Act does not automatically oust the Bhumidar from the land unless the land owner is ejected u/S 84 or 86A by specific order of RA, within three years of order under section 81.
The IP no.1 has not proved any such ejectment proceedings on record.

Therefore even when the application/contest of IP no.2-5, against proceedings u/S 81 i.e. Ex.IP2-5W1/1 was pending, by virtue of section 85 and 86A DLR Act the IP no. 2 to 5 became the Bhumidars of the land.

20. Except for Khasra Girdawaris IP no. 1 have not brought any material on record to show that IP no.2 to 5 were ejected from the land and the absence of BDO at the time of possession proceedings shows that IP no.2 to 5 were in possession of the land.
Hence in view of Hardwari Lal Supra, mere assertion of IP no.1 that it is the Bhumidar does not entitle it for compensation.

In view of findings given on issue no.1 above, the petition/claim of IPs No. 2 to 5 is allowed.
The compensation amount with accrued interest is to be apportioned a m o n g s t I P s N o .
